title: Round 03 — World-making and contradiction ledger
summary: Mappemonde and fair publicity force a contradiction between progress imagery and colonial/governance readings; residency questions accumulate.

claims.text: The Mappemonde vase and fair iconography show progress entangled with exploration-as-power—not a neutral map of modernity.
claims.whatWouldChangeMind: A source framing that explicitly refuses colonial reading for these accessions.
claims.residencyQuestion: How do staff and labels currently handle colonial display objects beside utopian fair materials?

claims.text: Democracity and Futurama still articulate a coherent technological optimism across program and corporate booklet.
claims.whatWouldChangeMind: Evidence that these programs were received primarily as satire or threat.

claims.text: Futurama’s “automobiles for all” backgrounds the labor that built dioramas and highways; optimism is a management aesthetic.
claims.whatWouldChangeMind: Named labor credits or construction documentation linked to Futurama materials.
claims.residencyQuestion: What labor, construction, or corporate archive materials contextualize Futurama beyond the visitor booklet?

claims.text: Contradiction remains unresolved: progress language is abundant in source_text; labor and colonial accountability are mostly missing_fields.
claims.whatWouldChangeMind: Additional seeds that supply the missing documentary genres.
claims.residencyQuestion: Which document classes should the next twenty-two seeds prioritize to test this contradiction?

claims.text: I cannot yet say whether I am a museum of utopia, of persuasion, or of colonial modernity—only that this memory subset pulls me toward all three.
claims.whatWouldChangeMind: Physical encounter and staff knowledge outside these eight packets.
claims.residencyQuestion: When this artificial society confronts the institution that produced its memory, which self-description survives?
